reading.body:
J-Curve Technologies is not a confirmed data center, and no power capacity can be attributed to it.

The entry rests on a single OpenStreetMap node tagged as a data center at coordinates in Tempe, Arizona. Reverse geocoding those coordinates returns only a building address on West 14th Street with no business name attached. No operator website, business registration, or press coverage naming J-Curve Technologies at that location could be confirmed, and the research status is recorded as exhausted. The name itself is more familiar as a finance term for a growth pattern than as a technology company.

For AI infrastructure questions this matters as a data quality point rather than a capacity point. Arizona has 56 mapped data center facilities, and only 4 of them publish power specifications, totaling 512 MW. A facility with no confirmed operator and no published specifications cannot be ranked against those four or counted toward state grid load. The map is a claim about a building, not evidence of servers.

What the data does not cover is equally clear. It does not establish that no data center exists at this address, only that none could be confirmed from public sources. It says nothing about the building's size, its power service, or its tenants. The nearest airport, Phoenix Sky Harbor, is 2.5 miles away, which describes geography and nothing about electrical infrastructure.
